environment: LIVE read-only subscription and queue aggregates; repository scheduler and pacing inspection
approvedScope: 160 enabled channel-history and observed-reply subscriptions; individual and group DMs excluded

steadyStateLowerBound.source: Near-live scheduler returns to windows of up to 15 minutes; each completed history window is gated on observed-parent reply checks. The approved internal Slack app currently uses a 30-second shared workspace request cooldown. The earlier real-source inventory observed 870 parent roots in 69 channels.
steadyStateLowerBound.additionalObservedParentChecks: The current reply scheduler rediscovers every saved parent root within a channel for each recurring history window. If all 870 retained roots are eligible at every 15-minute boundary, this adds up to 3,480 reply-window requests per hour before pagination. This is a design projection, not an observed provider-request count.

interpretation: The short-term successful job stream cannot establish sustainable 160-channel near-live capture. Even channel history alone exceeds the current shared pacing limit in steady state. Longer catch-up windows apply while a channel is more than one day behind, but the installed scheduler returns to 15-minute windows near live. Reply checks increase demand. A reviewed freshness/capacity design is required before Build 01 can claim unattended Slack convergence.
limits: The current queue is influenced by historical catch-up, retries and unfinished windows; the lower-bound model describes eventual 15-minute steady state, not measured hourly API traffic.
A successful or empty provider window does not establish full source coverage in still-lagged channels.
